revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule instead requires the first argument itself to be a fixed-size type or an expression of fixed-size type; it does not use the 2023 type-operator legality condition.
The 2012 text only predefines dimension 1 for integer, shortint, longint, and byte and does not include int or time in this array-query treatment.

The 2017 rule predefines dimension 1 only for integer, shortint, longint, and byte; it does not include int or time in this guarantee, unlike the 2023 rule covering all six predefined-width integer types.
The 2012 grammar accepts an array_identifier or data_type, whereas the 2023 grammar accepts a general array_expression or data_type.

The 2012 text explicitly guarantees the default `$error` for a failed immediate assert with no else; it does not state the 2023 centralized guarantee for assertion, assumption, expect, and wait_order action blocks.
The 2017 standard states the default `$error` action in the assertion action-block rules rather than consolidating it in Clause 20.
The 2012 grammar accepts any constant_expression, rather than requiring a package-scoped or hierarchical parameter identifier.
The 2012 task targets only a module and does not define `$unit` or `$root` argument behavior.
The 2017 task accepts only an optional hierarchical module identifier and reports that module's time unit and precision; it has no `$unit` or `$root` target behavior.
The 2012 no-argument form displays the current module's timescale, rather than the broader current design element rule.
The 2017 no-argument form reports the current module's timescale, whereas the 2023 rule generalizes the target to the current design element.
The 2012 format uses `module_name` and has no required `$unit` or `$root` displayed-name cases.
The 2017 required format names a module and does not define the 2023 `$unit` and `$root` design-element-name cases.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no `$stacktrace` task/function or call-stack retrieval guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no `$stacktrace` task/function or guarantee for retrieving and displaying/returning the current call stack.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no `$stacktrace` construct or syntax.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define the `$stacktrace` construct.
The 2012 rule applies settings to `%t` formats in modules following the invocation in source order, rather than stating a design-wide effect across all display and file-output tasks/functions.

The 2017 rule applies the `%t` settings to modules that follow the `$timeformat` call in source order (and also controls interactive delays), rather than stating a design-wide effect independent of source order.
IEEE 1800-2012 restricts `units_number` to -15 through 0 and does not impose the 2023 -15 through 2 range on both unit and precision arguments.
IEEE 1800-2017 restricts `units_number` to the encoded range 0 through -15; it does not allow 1 or 2 and does not impose that encoded range on `precision_number`.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no `$timeunit` or `$timeprecision` system functions or result encoding.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define `$timeunit` or `$timeprecision` retrieval functions or their integer result encoding.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no `$timeunit` or `$timeprecision` system-function syntax.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define the `$timeunit` or `$timeprecision` system-function constructs.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no `$timeunit` or `$timeprecision` query functions or target-selection behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no `$timeunit`/`$timeprecision` retrieval behavior for current, hierarchical, compilation-unit, or root targets.
